senses.definition: A cocktail made with gin or vodka and vermouth.
examples: Will you join us at six o’clock for martinis?
My boss is out on another of his three-martini lunches.

quotes.text: Even at Juneau's prices, ten dollars worth of martinis is a lot of liquor to drink in an hour.
quotes.reference: 1961 Jan, Robert Silverberg, Amazing Stories, page 26, column 2:

quotes.text:
Could any tiger
Drink martinis, smoke cigars,
And last as we do?
quotes.reference: c. 1963, W[ystan] H[ugh] Auden, “Symmetries & Asymmetries”, in Edward Mendelson, editor, Collected Poems, New York: Random House, published 1976, →ISBN, page 551:

quotes.text: He drank martini, played bridge in the club, and captured treaty-port life wickedly.
quotes.reference: 1997, Caroline Courtauld, May Holdsworth, The Hong Kong Story, Oxford, Oxon; New York, N.Y.: Oxford University Press, →ISBN, page 21:

quotes.text: I had the feeling that had he been a smoker he would have lit a cigarette at this moment. I suspected that once he had been a smoker, for he seemed as if he wished someone would offer him one. He drank martini instead.
quotes.reference: 2006, Joan [Elizabeth] Taylor, Conversations with Mr. Prain, Hoboken, N.J.: Melville House Publishing, →ISBN, page 172:

quotes.text: After the meal, they drank martini on the rocks in the lounge.
quotes.reference: 2007, Margaret S. Ngwa, Divine Love for Cleansing, Patron Publishing House, →ISBN, page 63:

senses.definition: (sometimes proscribed) Any cocktail served in a cocktail glass, often sweet or fruity and aimed at women.
examples: I love the chocolate martinis at Trendy Bar!
